theorems.statement: ∀ (F : Type*) [Field F] (A : Subring F) (ν : F → ℤ), (∀ f g : F, f ≠ 0 → g ≠ 0 → ν (f / g) = ν f - ν g) → (∀ f : F, f ≠ 0 → (f ∈ A ↔ 0 ≤ ν f)) → IsPrincipalIdealRing A
theorems.natural_summary: The zero ideal is principal. For a nonzero ideal, choose a nonzero element h minimizing its order converted to a natural number. Membership in A ensures these orders are nonnegative, so minimality also holds for integer orders. Every nonzero ideal element z then has ν(z/h) ≥ 0, hence z/h belongs to A and z is a multiple of h. Both ideal containments give I = (h). This matches the frozen parent-supplied proof.
